schemes.description: Final-year undergraduate business students, in self-selected groups of typically four, work on behalf of an external organisation that has identified a business problem or question, producing a group consultancy report and client presentation plus an individual literature review and reflective statement. Clients range from SMEs to multinationals and charities/community bodies; e.g. a July 2026 release reports four final-year students producing a tiered menu of recommendations for St Andrew's Parish Church, Spennymoor.

schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Programme-specific; module listed on named BA programme pages
schemes.credit_assessment: Group consultancy report (5,000 words) and client presentation 60%; individual critical literature review (3,000 words) + 2,000-word reflective statement 40%

profile_md: Northumbria runs employer-linked group projects through faculty-hosted routes rather than one institution-wide scheme. The strongest is the Newcastle Business School **Business Clinic**: NX9626 (final-year UG, self-selected groups of typically four working 'on behalf of an external organisation') and NX0479/NX0477 (PG Advanced Practice group consultancy for a host organisation). A July 2026 release documents a four-student team advising a parish church; the Clinic reports over 950 projects and 3,820+ students since 2013, mostly pro bono for SMEs, charities and larger firms. The Faculty of Engineering and Environment **Live Projects Hub** procures 12-week industry projects (around 100 businesses) which Advanced Practice Masters students deliver in small teams in the 60-credit Advanced Practice Semester (e.g. KB7056, 2026 listing). Computing offers KV5037 Computing Consultancy Project and 12-week undergraduate live projects, but group basis and compulsory status are unclear. The central experiential-learning page claims about 700 students per year complete a live project or clinic module (2021/22 audit) and the Projects page lists Film Live Briefs, Sport Outreach, Student Law Office and Building Advice Centre, but these lack module-level evidence of team working. No compulsory university-wide scheme found. Uncertain: whether the consultancy modules are core on each programme, and reach in sciences, social sciences and design.
gaps: Compulsory/optional status for NX9626, KV5037 and Advanced Practice Semester modules; Live Projects Hub page last reviewed 2023; NX0477 and London campus clinic only from search summaries; Film Live Briefs, Sport Event Management, design live-brief modules and the Computing school's 'every undergraduate' live-project claim not verified at module level; no module-level evidence found for Applied Sciences, Geography/Environmental Sciences or Social Sciences; further departmental instances likely. Reduced-depth mode: 10 searches, 9 page fetches.
